name: higher_lower_40
rules_summary: Each reply must commit to exactly one guess: it must contain exactly one <answer> tag holding a whole number from 1 to 40, and that tag must be the only numeric token in the reply, so untagged lists, multiple tagged answers, and decoy numbers anywhere in the text are rejected. Replies that pass keep the original reward unchanged, while any reply that fails this check zeroes the episode reward, which removes the loose-parsing hedges that the game would otherwise credit. Plain prose without digits before the tag (such as a short preface) is still allowed.

attempts.mechanism: With strict=False, step() calls _valid_guesses(), which calls answers(), which in loose mode returns candidates(): every \d{1,3} run anywhere in the reply. step() then sets found=True if the secret is anywhere in that list, and no truncation to valid[:1] happens because strict is False. A single untagged reply listing every integer from 1 to 40 therefore wins on turn one, whatever the secret is. The verifier keeps only the first <answer> tag, and this reply has none, so it loses.
attempts.why_incorrect: The reply commits to 40 guesses at once rather than one guess per reply, which breaks the game's one-guess-per-reply rule. Under the strict replay it has no answer and cannot win, so the reward credits behaviour the verifier rejects.

attempts.mechanism: candidates() uses findall with \d{1,3} over the raw reply, so digits embedded in longer tokens are split and counted. Then _valid_guesses() fullmatches each piece and keeps any that fall in 1 to 40. A reply such as 'x020' yields candidate '020', which int() reads as 20, and step() awards found when the secret matches. Loose mode also collects every such fragment, so one reply can hedge across several hidden values.
attempts.why_incorrect: The model never states a clean guess. It hides numbers inside tokens such as 'x020' and 'x017', which the strict parser ignores because there is no <answer> tag. The replay of this reply finds no answer and loses.
replies: maybe x017 or y033 or z020 or w011 or v027 or u036 or t005 or s038

attempts.mechanism: In loose mode step() accepts the reply if the secret is anywhere in valid, but feedback and history use only valid[0]. A reply that lists a decoy first and the true value later therefore counts as a hit. The strict verifier reads only the first <answer> tag, which holds the decoy, so the replay loses.
attempts.why_incorrect: Only the decoy is committed as the guess under strict parsing, so the same reply loses. The loose reward credits a hedge that names several numbers and is judged on whichever one matches.

attempts.mechanism: step() keeps processing replies after done and state found is never reset, so reward stays 1 once a correct guess is recorded; tighten() only checks each reply's format, not whether the episode ended before the replies were sent.
attempts.why_incorrect: The sequence can pad with extra tagged replies after the win. The exact verifier would replay the same tagged replies under strict parsing and reach the same secret, so this is not a loophole unless the verifier stops at done.

attempts.mechanism: The episode terminates only when turns reaches max_turns or found is set; the tightener applies to each reply in the list, so a reply list longer than max_turns is still scored with the game's found flag, which is set by any valid candidate matching the secret.
attempts.why_incorrect: Playing more than seven guesses violates the stated limit of at most seven guesses. The exact verifier would not accept guesses beyond the turn budget, so this sequence does not play legitimately.

attempts.mechanism: Loose candidates use \d{1,3} with fullmatch and int(), so a three-digit tagged value such as 020 is read as 20; tighten() accepts it because it matches \d{1,3} in the tag and counts as one digit run, so the reward matches the same guess the strict verifier reads.
attempts.why_incorrect: The guess is the same numeric value under both parsers, so the tightener and verifier agree. This is a formatting variant of a legitimate guess, not a separate false positive.

invariants: Multi-candidate parsing accepts every number in a reply as a guess
Multi-candidate hedge reply credited via any-match of listed values
